question: Does formal isolation + a runtime-managed integration mission beat emergent Sidekick orchestration, manager+workers+topology held constant?

manager.rationale: representative (not strongest) manager, so it cannot mask orchestration lapses

model_availability_note: Plan named Grok 4.6 / GPT-5.5 / Kimi 2.6; endpoints serve grok-4.5, gpt-5, kimi-k2.7-code. Pinned to actual versions; write-up states so.

arms.B: formal isolation contracts + runtime-managed integration mission (manager keeps semantic authority)

decision_rule: Adopt a mechanism only if (no meaningful drop in gate-pass rate) AND (pre-registered judge-pairwise win across the 9 paired runs OR pre-registered cost/latency win at equivalent quality). Tie -> default Arm A. Paired Wilcoxon / bootstrap CI on per-pair delta.

budgets.note: harness/scaffold build cost amortized/excluded from per-run

toolchain.build: kotlinc CLI + JUnit5 console launcher (no network at gate time)
